name: Farfisa
description: Farfisa combo organ listing copy, organized by production era and catalog model. Scoped to the Compact and FAST eras — the pre-integrated-circuit Farfisa models CEPCo specializes in restoring — per the Combo Organ Service page. Historical/technical details sourced from Wikipedia and cross-referenced combo organ references; anything not confidently verifiable was left out rather than guessed.

children.label: Combo Compact
children.copy:
Every Farfisa combo organ we restore for sale goes through the same meticulous process we're known for, with dozens of hours devoted to bringing each instrument to exceptional playing condition. We prioritize period-correct vintage components whenever possible, and turn to the best available reproduction parts when originals are no longer viable — always working to preserve the instrument's original character and unmistakable combo organ tone. The result is an organ that plays, sounds, and holds up better than it likely has since it left the factory.

This organ comes from Farfisa's original Compact series (1964-1969), the line that put Farfisa on the map as Vox's biggest combo organ rival. Compact-series organs are unusual for being only partially transistorized — the reverb circuit still runs on vacuum tubes — and they're built around germanium transistors, which give them a warmer, slightly less stable voice than the silicon-transistor organs that followed. It's the sound behind Sam the Sham & the Pharaohs' "Wooly Bully," the Grateful Dead's earliest lineup with Ron "Pigpen" McKernan, and Richard Wright's first Farfisa setup with Pink Floyd.

This is the original Compact model that started the line in 1964: a five-octave organ with 16' bass and strings, 8' flute, oboe, trumpet and strings, 4' flute, piccolo and strings, four vibrato settings, and three reverb settings through its built-in spring reverb.

Features:
- Cleaned, Lubricated & Restored Key Contacts and Switches
- Addressed Germanium Transistor Drift for Stable, In-Tune Voicing
- New Electrolytic Capacitors
- Fully Restored Power Supply
- Restored Tube Reverb Circuit
- Key Repair/Restoration (addressing cracked or degraded original keys)
- CEPCo's Expert Tuning & Voicing Setup
- Cleaned All Potentiometers, Switches & Connectors
- All Voltages Checked & Calibrated for Optimum Performance
- New Cables

children.label: Compact Duo
children.copy:
Every Farfisa combo organ we restore for sale goes through the same meticulous process we're known for, with dozens of hours devoted to bringing each instrument to exceptional playing condition. We prioritize period-correct vintage components whenever possible, and turn to the best available reproduction parts when originals are no longer viable — always working to preserve the instrument's original character and unmistakable combo organ tone. This organ comes from Farfisa's original Compact series (1964-1969), the line that put Farfisa on the map as Vox's biggest combo organ rival. Compact-series organs are unusual for being only partially transistorized — the reverb circuit still runs on vacuum tubes — and they're built around germanium transistors, which give them a warmer, slightly less stable voice than the silicon-transistor organs that followed. It's the sound behind Sam the Sham & the Pharaohs' "Wooly Bully," the Grateful Dead's earliest lineup with Ron "Pigpen" McKernan, and Richard Wright's first Farfisa setup with Pink Floyd.

The Compact Duo is the flagship of the Compact series: a dual-manual organ pairing a four-octave upper keyboard carrying the full range of Compact voices with a second four-octave manual dedicated to Dolce, Principale, and Ottava tones. Unlike the rest of the Compact line, the Duo doesn't run on its own — it connects via a multi-lead cable to a separate Farfisa F/AR power supply, preamp, and spring reverb unit (or alternatively a Farfisa TR/60 amplifier). It's the organ Richard Wright graduated to from his first Combo Compact during Pink Floyd's Piper at the Gates of Dawn era, and later the primary instrument for Van der Graaf Generator's Hugh Banton and Inspiral Carpets' Clint Boon.

children.label: FAST 2
children.copy:
Every Farfisa combo organ we restore for sale goes through the same meticulous process we're known for, with dozens of hours devoted to bringing each instrument to exceptional playing condition. We prioritize period-correct vintage components whenever possible, and turn to the best available reproduction parts when originals are no longer viable — always working to preserve the instrument's original character and unmistakable combo organ tone. The result is an organ that plays, sounds, and holds up better than it likely has since it left the factory.

This organ comes from Farfisa's FAST series ("Farfisa All-Silicon Transistor"), introduced at the 1968 NAMM show to sit alongside the Compact line. Where the Compact organs relied on germanium transistors, FAST organs use silicon transistors throughout, giving them a more stable, more reliably in-tune voice. They also swapped the Compact's wood-look cabinet for a metal case with a skin-plate finish, chrome folding legs, retractable carrying handles, and a removable music rack — a look clearly inspired by the Vox Continental that FAST organs were built to compete with.

This is the entry point of the FAST line: a four-octave organ (C to C) with a one-octave manual bass section, four 8' voice stops — flute, clarinet, reed, and strings — a two-speed vibrato, and an optional swell pedal.

- Cleaned, Lubricated & Restored Key Contacts and Switches
- New Electrolytic Capacitors
- Fully Restored Power Supply
- CEPCo's Expert Tuning & Voicing Setup
